info.title: PHP2Shell Labs API
info.summary: PHP2Shell exposure of a public host: a stage, a score, the one next step.
info.description: Open, no key. The exposure test makes one ordinary visit to the host you name plus PHP's credit query, and compares the advertised PHP version with the fixed releases for CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619. The exploit validation (validate: true, your consent) adds one small posted request and one large chunked request of about 48 MB and judges the answer; no exploit code is sent. Only test hosts you are allowed to connect to. Exposure results are kept for 24 hours and answered from that cache; a consented validation always runs fresh. Each result has a permanent share link and a PDF. Rate limits: 20 scans per caller address and 6 per host in any hour, 4 validations per caller address in any hour (429 with Retry-After). CORS is open (Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *). Source: https://github.com/manteiga-foundation/php2shell-labs (MIT).

post.description: Default response is a stream of newline-delimited JSON events (application/x-ndjson): start, fingerprint, one probe per question, validation (when consented), assessment, done, result, saved. Send `Accept: application/json` to wait for the end and receive one JSON object instead. A fresh cached exposure result (under 24 hours) is returned at once in both forms unless validate is true.

host.description: A host name, an http:// or https:// address, or an IP literal, optionally with :port. Ports 80 and 443 are scanned publicly; a bare name means 443, http:// means 80.

validate.description: Consent to the exploit validation: one request of about 48 MB to the host. The validation is skipped when nothing answered as PHP.

schema.description: One JSON event per line: {type: 'start'|'fingerprint'|'probe'|'validation'|'assessment'|'done'|'result'|'saved'|'error', ...}. The `result` event carries a ScanResult; `saved` carries the share id.

400.description: Not a public host, an unsupported port, or malformed input.

502.description: The engine could not complete the scan.

get.description: The same scan as POST with `Accept: application/json`, for a shell or an agent: `curl 'https://php2shell-labs.taptok-test.workers.dev/api/scan?host=example.com'`. Add `&validate=1` to consent to the validation.

400.description: Not a public host or malformed input.

get.summary: The five-page PDF report for a result

200.description: application/pdf, landscape Letter, five pages; Content-Disposition names the file. The first render after a quiet spell can take up to 20 seconds; later ones are cached.

get.summary: The human page for a result
get.description: Unlisted (noindex), with Open Graph preview. Share this with people; share the JSON with machines.

Stage.description: no-patch: PHP 5.4 through 8.1, inside the affected range on an end-of-life branch; only an upgrade removes the flaw. exposed: PHP 8.2 through 8.5.11, inside the affected range, a fixed release exists. hidden: PHP runs but hides its version; treated as exposed until known. not-affected: PHP older than 5.4. protected: a fixed release (8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, 8.2.35) or newer. not-php / unreachable: nothing answered as PHP, or no web server answered; no score.

cached.description: True when answered from a result under 24 hours old.

validate.description: Whether the caller consented to the validation for this scan.

findings.description: What the host said: reachable, status, serverSoftware, poweredBy, version {major, minor, patch} | null, versionText, egg (yes | no | error | untested), validation {verdict, baseline, payload, signature} | null, errors.

score.description: PHP2Shell exposure only, not general PHP hygiene: no-patch 15, exposed 35, hidden 50, not-affected 80, protected 100; null for not-php and unreachable. See /docs/scoring.

foundations.description: Four booleans (null when not measured): reachable, phpPresent, versionDisclosed, supportedBranch.

code.description: A stable code for the same refusal (for example port-not-allowed, rate-caller, rate-host, rate-validation, no-address, not-public, engine-busy, invalid-host), so a client can say it in its own language.

params.description: The values the message names: host, port, allowed, address.
